finding.claim: Pageant named-pipe client connects to a predictable pipe name without verifying the server's identity; if CryptProtectMemory fails silently, the suffix is a constant, so a local account can squat the pipe and impersonate the agent (low-medium, conditional on CryptProtectMemory failure, unverified on Windows).
finding.source: Precondition: Pageant not running and a local account can create \\.\pipe\pageant.<user>.<suffix> first. Name built from username (UPN local part) plus SHA-256 of CryptProtectMemory output.
finding.sink: ClientOptions::open(&pipe_name) at namedpipes.rs:33; returned stream is trusted as the SSH agent.

trace.note: CryptProtectMemory result discarded (let _ =); comment says errors explicitly ignored
SHA-256 suffix; constant zero-padded plaintext if encryption failed
open pipe with no server owner/SID check
stream returned to caller as agent

finding.guards_checked: CROSS_PROCESS flag and hashing only obscure the name, they are not secrets. No server process owner/SID verification. Pipe name includes username, which is not a control. Silent CryptProtectMemory failure is the weak point. Impact: squatter sees agent requests (identities, session-bound sign requests) and can return forged identity lists or deny service; cannot forge signatures.

finding.claim: Org policy violation: the Windows username (PII) is written to debug logs via the pipe name.
finding.source: get_username() at namedpipes.rs:50 returns the account name (UPN local part or SAM name).

trace.note: pipe name logged at debug level

finding.guards_checked: Debug level only. Org policy forbids logging PII at any level, so this is still a violation. Exploitability is none; severity depends on who can read debug logs.

finding.claim: FindWindowW("Pageant","Pageant") can be satisfied by any process on the same desktop creating a window with that class and title, so a squatter receives the WM_COPYDATA request and the mapping name (low severity; same-desktop code is typically same-user).
finding.source: Any same-desktop process can register a top-level window with class and title Pageant.
finding.sink: SendMessageA(hwnd, WM_COPYDATA, ...) at wmmessage.rs:217-224, carrying the request mapping name in lpData.

trace.note: MemoryMap::new creates PageantRequest<cookie> mapping and writes request
synchronous SendMessageA to whatever window was found

finding.guards_checked: 64-bit random cookie prevents predicting the mapping name in advance, but the name is disclosed in the message so a squatter can read the request. Mapping uses the current user's default DACL. SendMessageA is synchronous, so a hung squatter also blocks the client. Not verified by execution.

finding.claim: MapViewOfFile result is not checked for failure, so a failed map leads to writes or reads through a null base pointer (robustness; needs resource exhaustion). ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS on CreateFileMappingW is also not detected (hardening only).
finding.source: Resource exhaustion or OS failure of MapViewOfFile.
finding.sink: MemoryMap::write at wmmessage.rs:150-154 and read at wmmessage.rs:165-171 dereference self.view.Value.add(pos).

trace.note: MapViewOfFile result stored without null check

finding.guards_checked: is_invalid() check on the file mapping handle. Length checks in write/read bound offsets but not the base pointer. Random cookie makes name collision infeasible.

finding.claim: Unbounded read buffer: the length prefix is not checked against _AGENT_MAX_MSGLEN before buffering, so the buffer grows until len+4 bytes arrive; len+4 can overflow on 32-bit targets (hardening; writer is the local client).
finding.source: Local SSH client writes a 4-byte length prefix up to u32::MAX.
finding.sink: buf accumulation at wmmessage.rs:36-46 and split_to(len + 4) at :47.

trace.note: map.write rejects over 8192 only after full buffering

finding.guards_checked: map.write checks length (wmmessage.rs:139-142) but only after buffering. Duplex capacity limits writer pressure only indirectly. Writer is the local client, so the impact is low.
